ios.desc:
LingoPop is a word association puzzle game that helps you learn vocabulary in 195+ languages. Connect four words that belong to the same category—quick to learn, fun to play, and perfect for a daily brain workout.

HOW IT WORKS
• Each puzzle shows 16 words. Find the four that share a common theme or category.
• Tap to select, tap Submit to check. Correct groups stay; wrong guesses cost a mistake.
• Play in any language you’re learning. Puzzles are generated so you practice real vocabulary in context.

FEATURES
• 195+ languages — from Spanish and French to Japanese, Arabic, and many more
• Daily puzzles — fresh challenges every day
• Streaks & milestones — build a daily streak and hit 7-, 14-, 30-, 60-, and 100-day goals
• Streak freezes (Premium) — 2 freezes so you don’t lose your streak when you miss a day
• Activity calendar — see your play history at a glance
• Leaderboard — sign in, set a username, and compete with others
• Progress tracking — stats, wins, and languages played (with Premium)
• First-time guide — clear “How to play” so anyone can start in seconds

FREE & PREMIUM
• Free: play a set number of puzzles per day, build streaks, and climb the leaderboard
• Premium: unlimited daily puzzles, 2 streak freezes, detailed stats, and priority puzzle generation

Perfect for language learners, puzzle fans, and anyone who wants a quick, satisfying word game. Download LingoPop and connect words—one puzzle at a time.

quotes.text:
I’ve been building a small side project called LingoPop — a word-connection game inspired by puzzle games like NYT Connections, but for language lovers.

The twist: it works in 195+ languages. 
You connect words that belong to the same category (slang, cooking actions, mental processes, etc.), and the categories adapt to the language you choose.

I actually built it for a personal reason too. I’m an expat living in Berlin, my native language is Vietnamese, and I wanted a more playful way to practice German and Italian. I also play the game in English, which sometimes turns out to be harder than expected

So I’m curious to ask this community:

How many languages do you speak?
Now try to prove it by playing LingoPop in those languages.

I’d love to hear:

Which language felt the hardest?

Which word groups surprised you?

Does the difficulty change depending on the language?

Always happy to get feedback from fellow builders and language nerds!
